news.title: Times Green Energy (India) Limited Announces Management Changes
news.body: Times Green Energy (India) Limited announced that the Board of Directors the Company at their meeting held on January 20, 2026 and approved Cessation of Mrs. Padma Priyanka Vangala as the Non-Executive Independent Director with effect from October 21, 2025 upon completion of her current term. Appointment of Mr. Mahavir Kumar Jain as the Company Secretary and Compliance Officer of the Company with effect from January 20, 2026. Mr. Mahavir Kumar Jain is an Associate Member of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (ICSI). With over 8 years of experience in legal and regulatory roles, he is a Company Secretary, bringing expertise in corporate governance and compliance. Mr. Mahavir Kumar Jain is not related to any Director of the Company.

news.title: Times Green Energy (India) Limited Announces Resignation of Company Secretary and Compliance Officer Abhishek Reddy Rachur, Effective January 1, 2026
news.body: Times Green Energy (India) Limited announced that CS Abhishek Reddy Rachur has tendered his resignation as the Company Secretary and Compliance Officer of the company with effect from January 1, 2026. The resignation was accepted by the Board of Directors on January 3, 2026. The noting of resignation will be taken at the ensuing Board Meeting of the company and the appointment of subsequent Company Secretary and Compliance Officer shall be intimated to the Stock Exchange in due course of time. The resignation was submitted in order to pursue better career opportunities.

news.title: New major risk - Shareholder dilution
news.body: The company's shareholders have been substantially diluted in the past year. Increase in shares outstanding: 68% This is considered a major risk. Shareholder dilution occurs when there is an increase in the number of shares on issue that is not proportionally distributed between all shareholders. Often due to the company raising equity capital or some options being converted into stock. All else being equal, if there are more shares outstanding then each existing share will be entitled to a lower proportion of the company's total earnings, thus reducing earnings per share (EPS). While dilution might not always result in lower EPS (like if the company is using the capital to fund an EPS accretive acquisition) in a lot cases it does, along with lower dividends per share and less voting power
